items.title: Show HN: Visual heat map of AI news updated hourly
items.desc: description: An interactive map of the AI companies, models, products, people and ideas getting the most attention in Englishlanguage news over the last 7 days. × × About Jag's AI Map An interactive map of the AI companies, models, products, people, hardware and ideas that are getting the most attention in AI news and developer communities. Bigger, closer to the centre and more connected means more talked about. Browse the articles The Articles button (top right) opens a scrollable archive of every article behind the map — the last 30 days, grouped by source, newest first. Pick a source on the left to see just its stories; click any headline to open it in a new tab. The small red number under the button counts how many new articles were discovered in the last hour. How heat works Every story adds heat to each entity it mentions, weighted by source and popularity (Hacker News points, Hugging Face upvotes, GitHub stars). Heat cools with a 24\hour halflife, so the map reflects the last few days of a 7day window. Links join entities that appear in the same stories. Week covers 7 days with a 24hour halflife; Today covers 24 hours with a 6hour halflife and compares with 6 hours earlier. Breaking (orange name, pulsing ring) means an entity got at least 2 stories and 2.5× more attention in the last 6 hours than in the 6 hours before. New (orange ring) marks entities first spotted this week; ↑ means heat is at least 1.5× what it was 24 hours earlier, ↓ that it has cooled. Topics are drawn as diamonds; the hottest topic is filled orange and its closest connections are outlined. Sources this run Built independently; inspired by [AI MAP by carlwow](https://aimap.goodcase.ai). Not affiliated with any company shown. Graph rendering by [D3](https://d3js.org) (ISC licence).
items.author: jnaina
items.descZh: 该产品是一个交互式AI地图工具，用于可视化AI公司、模型、产品、人物和想法在英语新闻及开发者社区中的关注度，数据基于最近7天的动态更新。核心功能包括通过实体的大小、中心位置和连接度反映热度，并提供文章存档浏览、来源筛选和实时新文章计数。亮点在于其精细的热度算法，例如热度以24小时半衰期冷却，Breaking标记要求实体在6小时内获得至少2个故事和2.5倍于之前6小时的关注增长，同时支持Week和Today不同时间窗口的比较。适用场景涵盖帮助AI从业者、投资者和研究者快速识别行业热点、跟踪趋势和发现新兴机会。

items.title: Show HN: Vramkit – measuring LLM weight and KV-cache compression on a MacBook
items.desc: description: VRAM compression for LLM inference, measured on a MacBook: lossless weight codec (33% vs 4bit on real Qwen weights, beats zstd) + dropin PyTorch KVcache compression. Key finding: quantize KV keys perCHANNEL (not pertoken) > int8 KV nearlossless, +0.1% real perplexity at 2x. ROCm/CUDA/MPS/CPU. SRKRZ23/vramkit image: https://opengraph.githubassets.com/c691b58326c64ceb5e1c98fa6abe8acdc82db507c514ae0065dd3ec46b078541/SRKRZ23/vramkit title: GitHub SRKRZ23/vramkit: VRAM compression for LLM inference, measured on a MacBook: lossless weight codec (33% vs 4bit on real Qwen weights, beats zstd) + dropin PyTorch KVcache compression. Key finding: quantize KV keys perCHANNEL (not pertoken) > int8 KV nearlossless, +0.1% real perplexity at 2x. ROCm/CUDA/MPS/CPU. <DOCTYPE html [Skip to content](startofcontent) You signed in with another tab or window. Reload to refresh your session. You signed out in another tab or window. Reload to refresh your session. You switched accounts on another tab or window. Reload to refresh your session. Dismiss alert {{ message }} [](/SRKRZ23/vramkit) main [Branches](/SRKRZ23/vramkit/branches)[Tags](/SRKRZ23/vramkit/tags) Go to file Code Open more actions menu Latest commit History [9 Commits](/SRKRZ23/vramkit/commits/main/) 9 Commits Folders and files Name Name Last commit message Last commit date [bench](/SRKRZ23/vramkit/tree/main/bench "bench") [bench](/SRKRZ23/vramkit/tree/main/bench "bench") [docs](/SRKRZ23/vramkit/tree/main/docs "docs") [docs](/SRKRZ23/vramkit/tree/main/docs "docs") [vramkit](/SRKRZ23/vramkit/tree/main/vramkit "vramkit") [vramkit](/SRKRZ23/vramkit/tree/main/vramkit "vramkit") [.gitignore](/SRKRZ23/vramkit/blob/main/.gitignore ".gitignore") [.gitignore](/SRKRZ23/vramkit/blob/main/.gitignore ".gitignore") [POST.md](/SRKRZ23/vramkit/blob/main/POST.md "POST.md") [POST.md](/SRKRZ23/vramkit/blob/main/POST.md "POST.md") [README.md](/SRKRZ23/vramkit/blob/main/README.md "README.md") [README.md](/SRKRZ23/vramkit/blob/main/README.md "README.md") View all files Repository files navigation vramkit — measurable VRAM compression for LLM inference Two techniques to cut the two things that eat GPU memory during LLM inference — the model weights and the KVcache — each with a runnable benchmark behind every number. Weight numbers are lossless, bitexact verified. KV numbers are validated as real endtask perplexity on a real model, not a proxy. No handwaving. Why it matters: at inference scale, VRAM is the binding cost. Shrinking weights and KVcache directly cuts GPU count / lets bigger context fit — the exact lever hyperscalers spend heavily on. Everything here was built and measured entirely on a MacBook (Apple Silicon, CPU torch) — you do not need a datacenter GPU to reproduce it. 1\. Weight codec — lossless, beats general compressors A fromscratch 32bit range coder with a 2D adaptive context model (each 4bit weight conditioned on its left + up neighbours) — structure byteoriented compressors (zstd/xz) can't see. On REAL LLM weights (Qwen2.50.5B, self_attn.o_proj, int4 — python3 bench/validate_real_weights.py <model.safetensors): method bits/weight vs raw 4bit raw 4bit packed 4.000 — zstd 19 2.717 −32.1% xz 9e 2.708 −32.3% vramkit (2D ctx) 2.676 −33.1% Lossless (bitexact verified), −33% vs raw 4bit, beating zstd19 by 1.5% / xz9e by 1.2% on real quantized LLM weights — sitting on the 2D entropy floor. Across every weighttensor type of Qwen2.50.5B it averages 2.92 bits/weight, −27% vs raw 4bit, lossless, beating zstd19 on 4 of 5 — a general property of quantized LLM weights, not one lucky tensor. (On synthetic lowrank data the edge over zstd is smaller, \~−22%; the realweights number is the one that counts.) 2\. KVcache compression — get the quantization axis right The headline finding, and the reason to read this repo: keys and values want different quantization axes. Keys carry a few persistent perchannel outliers (massiveactivation dims). A pertoken scale lets those outliers dominate and crushes every other value. A perchannelscale (one per feature dim, across tokens) fixes it. Values are wellbehaved per token. Endtask validation — real perplexity, measured on a MacBook (python3 bench/validate_ppl_mac.py, Qwen2.50.5B, KV compression applied to every layer's K/V via forward hooks, averaged over 4 disjoint windows of real prose, baseline perplexity ≈ 18): scheme memory Δ ppl, keys preRoPE Δ ppl, keys postRoPE (standard cache) int8, pertoken K & V (the naive way) 2.0× +4.6% +3.7% int8, perCHANNEL K + pertoken V 2.0× +0.10% (nearlossless ✅) +0.13% ✅ int8 K (perchan) + int4 V (pertoken) 2.67× +1.4% +1.6% int4, perCHANNEL K + pertoken V 4.0× +25.6% +27.4% Pre vs postRoPE keys (keys both, thanks to Hakob Arzumanyan on the AMD Developer Community for catching it): hooking k_proj quantizes keys _before_ RoPE, but a standard transformers cache stores them _after_ RoPE (past_key_values.update receives rotated keys). The postRoPE column quantizes exactly what the cache stores (the model's apply_rotary_pos_emb is wrapped; the script prints the call count so a silent noop can't pass as "lossless"). int8 perchannel keys hold in both places (+0.10% vs +0.13%), so the 2× result applies to a dropin postRoPE cache. At int4, preRoPE is slightly better (+25.6% vs +27.4%), consistent with KVQuant's choice to cache preRoPE keys — but int4 keys regress either way. The whole game is the key axis. Perchannel int8 keys make the KV cache 2× smaller for +0.1% perplexity — genuinely nearfree. The naive pertoken scheme most quick implementations reach for costs +4.6% at the same memory. Pushing values to int4 buys 2.67× for \~1.4%; int4 keys still regress hard (+25.6%), so int4 is a valuesonly lever here. Honesty note: an earlier version of this repo reported KV quality as cosine similarity and as a perplexity number from a _repetitive_ eval corpus, which made int8 look free (+0.02%) and hid the pertoken key problem. cossim overstated quality (pertoken vs perchannel keys differ b
items.author: sardor_r1
items.descZh: 随着大语言模型（LLM）推理规模化，显存（VRAM）已成为限制推理成本和上下文长度的瓶颈，vramkit提供了一套高度可量化的显存压缩解决方案。其核心包含两大技术：一种基于2D自适应上下文模型的无损权重编解码器，以及一种即插即用的PyTorch KV缓存量化方案。在权重压缩方面，它在真实Qwen模型上实现了平均2.92 bits/weight（较原始4位量化降低27%），体积缩减达33%，无损表现超越了zstd和xz等通用压缩器。KV缓存压缩的核心在于采用逐通道（per-channel）而非逐token的int8量化，能在实现2倍显存压缩的同时，将真实困惑度（perplexity）增量控制在0.1%以内，达到近乎无损的效果。该工具支持ROCm、CUDA、MPS和CPU，所有基准测试均在MacBook本地完成，适用于从云端GPU优化到本地端侧大模型高效部署的多种显存敏感场景。
items.quote: Perchannel int8 keys 可使 KV cache 缩小一半，而困惑度仅增加 0.1% —— 几乎是零成本的优化。

items.title: Show HN: Death Plan Switch, a self-hosted dead man's switch for solo devs
items.desc: Hi HN, I'm Peter Bishop and I've been working in graphics and web tech for over 25yrs. I've recently launched Death Plan Switch to solve a major problem in my succession plan. What if I go missing or die? The right people are told and my business can continue to operate for my clients
items.author: romeo19361
items.descZh: Peter Bishop 是一位拥有超过 25 年图形和网页技术经验的资深从业者，他推出 Death Plan Switch 是为了解决企业主突然离世后业务可能中断的难题。该产品的核心功能是预先设定在创始人去世或失踪时，能自动通知指定的联系人，并确保业务得以继续为 clients 服务。其亮点在于将 succession plan 从一个模糊的构想转化为一个可执行、可依赖的自动化方案，从而保障业务的连续性。这尤其适用于企业主、自由职业者以及任何希望确保自己身故后事业和客户利益能得到妥善安排的人。
items.quote: 如果我失踪或死亡怎么办？合适的人会被告知，我的业务可以继续为客户运营。

items.descZh: Rouler 是一款 Windows 平台的网络流量路由工具，旨在帮助用户在多个网络接口之间灵活引导流量。其核心功能是通过自定义规则，将不同应用程序的流量分配到特定的网络连接上，实现精细化的网络控制。亮点在于支持同时运行多个 VPN 客户端，例如 Tailscale、Mullvad 和 OpenVPN，并能为 Slack 等应用指定通过 OpenVPN 连接发送流量，而 Chrome 等浏览器则通过其他接口访问，提升网络灵活性和安全性。该工具适用于需要复杂网络配置的场景，如多 VPN 并发、应用级流量隔离或混合网络环境优化。

items.author: IreneAI
items.descZh: Agent Memory Leaderboard 是一个开创性的开放冠军赛，旨在为代理记忆系统提供中立、可重复和公平的评估平台。其核心功能是举办 Agent Memory Challenge 2026 Cycle 2，通过文本、编码和多模态三个赛道，测试代理的长期记忆能力，重点在于检索正确证据、识别变化和避免过时上下文。亮点包括吸引超过50个团队参与，编码赛道包含150个软件任务，用于评估代理在嘈杂环境中保持记忆准确性的性能。该平台适用于研究人员和开发团队，帮助他们验证和优化代理记忆系统，尤其适用于需要长期依赖历史信息的复杂场景。
items.quote: 长期记忆不仅仅是存储更多历史。这是关于检索正确的证据，认识到发生了什么变化，并避免陈旧的背景

items.desc: description: Send gift cards to survey participants, study subjects, employees, or customers — one at a time, from a spreadsheet, or by API. Recipients pick from hundreds of brands. You pay face value, nothing else. title: SendReward — Send gift cards at face value. No fees. image: https://sendreward.com/brand/ogimage.png Send gift cards to anyone. Pay face value. Reward survey respondents, study participants, employees, or customers. Send one from the dashboard, thousands from a spreadsheet, or from your own software with one API call. Recipients pick from hundreds of brands. You pay exactly the card's value — no fees. [Try it free in test mode](/app/signup.php) [See how it works](ways) Send oneCampaignAPI Recipient maria@example.com Amount $25.00 Message Thanks for finishing our survey Send $25.00 nowDeducted at face value · refunded if undeliverable Recipients · surveyq3.xlsx emailnameamount maria@…Maria25 ben@…Ben25 cat@…Cat50 \+ 1,240 more Validation 1,243 valid · 0 problems · 2 duplicates merged · total $31,075 Launch campaignFunds reserved up front · pause or cancel any time curl https://sendreward.com/api/v1/rewards \ H "Authorization: Bearer sr_live_…" \ d '{"recipient_email":"maria@example.com", "amount":25,"message":"Thanks for finishing our survey"}' → 201 Created { "id": "rw_7f3a…", "status": "sent" } Idempotent, webhooks, sandbox. [Docs →](/docs/) R Rewards to maria@example.com You've received a $25 reward Thanks for finishing our survey $25.00 Choose how you'd like to receive it: AmazonVisaTargetStarbucksPayPal\+ hundreds more Arrives in seconds. No account needed to redeem. A $10 thankyou, in someone's inbox thirty seconds after they earned it. That's the whole product. Three ways to send No developer required. Every route ends the same way: an email with a gift card the recipient chooses. We flag bad rows and duplicates before anything goes out. Send now or schedule it, watch progress, download results. POST /api/v1/rewards { "recipient_email": "maria@…", "amount": 25 } → 201 { "status": "sent" } Integrate by API One HTTP call from your survey tool, app, or script. Idempotency keys, webhooks, and a sandbox that never emails anyone. [Read the docs →](/docs/) 1 Add funds by bank transfer or card 2 Send — dashboard, spreadsheet, or API 3 Track sent, delivered, and redeemed. Export for accounting. What recipients can choose from You send a value; the recipient picks the brand. Gift cards, prepaid cards, and payout options from the names people actually want — Amazon, Visa, Target, Starbucks, and hundreds more. 74 popular brands Amazon Gift card Visa Prepaid card PayPal PayPal Target Gift card Walmart Gift card Sam's Club Gift card Best Buy Gift card Home Depot Gift card Lowe's Gift card Starbucks Gift card Dunkin' Gift card Chipotle Gift card …and hundreds more, including charity donations and prepaid Visa and Mastercard cards. Recipients choose at redemption — you don't have to decide for them.[See them in your dashboard](/app/signup.php) Pricing A $10 reward costs $10. Face valueand nothing else Platform fee$0 Perreward fee$0 Monthly subscription$0 Sandbox testingFree, unlimited Minimum topup$20 Reward size$1 – $1,000 How is that possible? We buy gift cards at volume rates. The difference between what we pay and face value is our margin, so we never need to charge you a fee on top. Bank transfers are free to you. Card topups add a 3% + $0.30 processing surcharge, which is exactly what the card networks charge us — we don't mark it up. Built for Anyone who needs to pay people small amounts, quickly, without collecting bank details — whether or not they have a developer. Surveys and market research Export respondents to a spreadsheet and send in one campaign, or trigger from your survey tool by API. Clinical and academic studies Participant compensation from a coordinator's spreadsheet, with a results export your finance office can reconcile. Health and wellness apps Milestone and adherence rewards, triggered from your own logic. Referral and review programs Pay the referrer the moment the condition is met. Employee recognition Birthdays, anniversaries, spot bonuses — sent one at a time from the dashboard, or in a monthly campaign. Customer service recovery A $20 apology from a support macro beats a coupon code. Questions Do I need a developer? No. Sign up, add funds, and send from the dashboard — one recipient at a time or a whole spreadsheet. The API is there if you want to automate it later. What can recipients choose from? Hundreds of brands including Amazon, Visa and Mastercard prepaid cards, Target, Starbucks, DoorDash, PayPal, and charity donations. The recipient picks at redemption; you don't have to decide for them. Do recipients need an account? No. They get an email, click, choose a brand, and receive the card. Nothing to install or sign up for. What if the email bounces or is never opened? You'll see the status in your dashboard and via webhook. Unclaimed rewards can be reviewed and handled with support. Can I send in bulk? Yes. Upload a CSV or Excel file as a campaign — up to 10,000 recipients with individual amounts and messages. We validate every row, hold the funds, and send at a steady rate so you can pause or cancel midway. Or loop over the API. Can I schedule sends? Campaigns can be scheduled for a date and time. Funds are reserved when you schedule, so the campaign can't fail for lack of balance when it fires. Can I try it without spending money? Every account starts with $1,000 of test balance. Test mode works everywhere — the dashboard, campaigns, and the API — and behaves exactly like live except nothing
